name: EWA World Heavyweight Championship
notes: The fed's own Hall of Champions index links a World Heavyweight Championship history page (ewaefed.ucoz.com/index/world_heavyweight_championship/0-32) that was never captured.
epitaph: The fed's own top belt, and the one it built its newsdesk around: Buzzsaw carried it through the spring of 2011 and booked himself airtime for an announcement the fed spent a fortnight speculating about, and Crimson Blaze chased it until he issued a statement saying he could not get the job done. Justin Marsham beat Buzzsaw for it at Retaliation in a Stairway to Death match, and used his first Shatter Point as champion to promise a title match every week rather than only at pay-per-view — opening with a shot for Crimson Blaze the following week.

name: EWA International Championship
notes: The fed's own Hall of Champions index links an International Championship history page (ewaefed.ucoz.com/index/international_championship/0-33) that was never captured.
epitaph: One of the four championships the fed's own Hall of Champions indexes, and one of the three it advertised to applicants alongside the World Heavyweight and Tag Team belts. Buck Evans is the only holder the surviving record names, still champion as of Shatter Point 7/5/11 after Big Nasty's attack put challenger Alexander Slate out of action; Cassandra Avery won a three-way over Thrax and Ruthless Aggression the same night to become his next number-one contender.

name: EWA Underground Championship
notes: The fed's own Hall of Champions index links an Underground Championship history page (ewaefed.ucoz.com/index/underground_championship/0-34) that was never captured.
epitaph: A 24/7 belt with rules of its own: anyone on the roster except the World Champion could challenge for it at any time by sending the word “Challenge” to the front office, first come first served, and it was defended out of a board only its own champion could read. El Pablo won it on Shatter Point in May 2011; the fed's own record shows it changing hands twice more inside two months, to Chris Johnson at Retaliation and then to a surprise-entrant Waylon Krews mid-way through an unrelated tag match on Shatter Point 7/5/11. The fed called it innovative in its own recruiting copy.

name: EWA Tag Team Championship
notes: The fed's own Hall of Champions index links a Tag Team Championship history page (ewaefed.ucoz.com/index/tag_tream_championship/0-35) that was never captured.
epitaph: Advertised to new applicants alongside the World Heavyweight and International belts, and indexed on the fed's own Hall of Champions. The teams the fed signed for it — NeXtreme, the Southern Express — filed with it in mid-2011, but it was the Home Town Heroes (Mark Jackson and Jun Yao) who won it first, at Retaliation, over Total Mayhem and a Sons of Ohio/Wreckers pairing — and spent the rest of the held record fending off the Mayhem brothers, who turned on them the very night they won the belts.
